item.title: Mentoring two junior developers: what actually helped
item.description: For most of this year I’ve been mentoring two junior developers on our team. I had done bits of this before, a code review here, an explanation there, but never as an actual responsibility for someone’s growth. Here’s what I think worked, and what I’d do differently. Real work, sized right The temptation is to give juniors “safe” work: small bugs, copy changes, tests nobody needs. It’s safe, and it teaches almost nothing, because there’s no real decision in it.

item.title: What I learned as the first in-house engineer
item.description: At the end of this month I’m leaving HolaLuz. I joined when the company was small and its software was built by an external agency. I was the first engineer hired to own it in-house. When I leave, there’s a team of developers, a CI pipeline, infrastructure as code, and a system that fails in smaller and more boring ways than it used to. This is not a goodbye post, it’s notes for myself on what I would tell someone starting in the same position.
